studies.title: Sequence Knowledge vs Property Prediction Error in Claude Mythos 5.2 and Masked Protein Language Models
studies.authors: Logan Hallee (Synthyra) and collaborators
studies.code_and_data_released: All prompts, answers, tables, and scripts released in repository.

methods.datasets: 118 sequences from FLIP2 and FGFR2: 6 dataset parents (amylase, IRED, NucB, TrpB, PDZ3, FGFR2), 100 Rhomax queries (48 scored by Mythos 5.2), and 12 shuffled negative controls.
methods.evaluation_protocol: 15%, 50%, and 85% of residues masked at shared positions across all models. Masked pLMs scored by single-site pseudo-log-likelihood (PPLL) and masked recovery; Mythos 5.2 scored by share of masked residues restored across 6 rotated prompt files with no overlap across levels.
methods.controls_included: Shuffled sequence copies (12 sequences), most-common visible residue baseline, and partial Spearman controlling for distance of true absorption maximum from the median.
methods.compute_and_tools: Single text prompt per batch via audited subagents (Read prompt, Write answer only) at low effort; ESMC/ESM-2 run in Docker on oracle_gh200.
methods.metrics: Masked residue recovery accuracy at 15/50/85% masking; Spearman correlation (2,000 bootstrap draws) between sequence knowledge and absolute absorption-maximum prediction error (nm).
methods.wet_lab_protocol: None (computational memorization and error correlation audit).

key_results.benchmark: 48 natural rhodopsins at 15% / 50% / 85% masking (+12 shuffled controls)
key_results.notes: All-or-nothing sequence recall: Mythos returned 34/48, 32/48, and 23/48 rhodopsins at >=90% accuracy (and FGFR2 100% at 50% mask), whereas no pLM reached 90% on any rhodopsin.

key_results.benchmark: 48 rhodopsins (Mythos) / 100 rhodopsins (pLMs) absorption-maximum error
key_results.notes: Memorizing a sequence does not predict Mythos's property-prediction accuracy (8 never-recited rhodopsins have 3.5 nm median error vs 4.0 nm for 19 always-recited).

temporal_cutoff.evidence: Explicitly designed as a direct sequence-memorization measurement on public pre-cutoff proteins (including confirming FGFR2 sequence is memorized even though its Nov 2026 assay is post-cutoff).

homology_overlap.evidence: Experiment record explicitly notes Rhomax queries include variants of shared wild-types, so the 48 sequences are not fully independent and bootstrap CIs are slightly narrow; masked recovery mixes exact sequence recall with family knowledge.

cross_modal_literature_recall.evidence: Direct target of measurement; rotated prompt files prevent cross-level leakage within a batch.

preprocessing_artifacts.evidence: Shuffled controls confirm zero composition shortcut (0.096-0.107 vs 0.110 majority guess); length mismatches audited (1,005/1,005 right length, 1 visible residue altered).

downstream_oracle_filtering.evidence: Direct masked sequence completion without external oracle.

compute_and_tool_asymmetry.evidence: No tools allowed (transcripts audited); identical masked positions across Mythos 5.2 and all four pLMs.

baseline_fairness.evidence: Evaluates ESMC-300M/600M/6B and ESM-2 650M on both exact PPLL and identical multi-mask completion.

data_and_wetlab_transparency.evidence: All prompts, answers, and per-sequence CSVs released; power limit transparently stated (n=48 detects |r| >= 0.4).

studies.takeaway: Claude Mythos 5.2 reconstructs natural rhodopsins at 91%/76%/57% accuracy under 15%/50%/85% masking (far above ESMC-6B's 59%/54%/13%, and 100% on FGFR2 at 50% masking), confirming strong sequence memorization. Yet sequence recall does not predict Mythos's absorption-maximum error (Spearman -0.15, CI -0.41 to +0.13), showing sequence recall and property accuracy are distinct.

studies.title: General-Purpose Language Models vs Ridge on Protein Language Models (FLIP2 and Post-Cutoff FGFR2)

Claude Fable 5.2 (API, low and high effort)
plm_baselines: One-hot + zero-shot ridge (ESMC-6B, ESMC-600M, ESMC-300M, ESM-2 650M)
Zero-shot masked marginals / PPLL (ESMC-6B, ESMC-600M, ESMC-300M, ESM-2 650M)

methods.metrics: Mean Spearman rank correlation across splits with 95% paired bootstrap intervals (2,000 draws), plus NDCG, top-decile ROC AUC, PR AUC, balanced MCC, and within-stratum Spearman.
methods.wet_lab_protocol: None (retrospective FLIP2 and prospective post-cutoff MaveDB evaluation).

key_results.benchmark: FLIP2 (16 splits, k=256, first 100 queries)
key_results.notes: Pre-specified tie (3 wins, 3 losses, 10 undecided). Excluding Rhomax (driven by prior knowledge), Mythos scores 0.36 vs ridge 0.38 (-0.02, -0.07 to +0.03). Fable 5.2 API also ties best ridge on all 300 queries (0.365 vs 0.355).

key_results.benchmark: Post-cutoff FGFR2 MaveDB (2 splits, k=256, first 100 queries)
key_results.notes: Assay published 2026-11-20 after June 2026 model cutoff. Tie holds without measurement leakage (though FGFR2 sequence itself is known; cipher drops fgfr2/random from 0.662 to 0.342).

key_results.benchmark: FLIP2 (16 splits) & FGFR2 (2 splits), k=256
key_results.llm_model: Equal-weight rank average (Mythos 5.2 + best ESMC ridge)
key_results.baseline_score: +0.063 (+0.033 to +0.092) over Mythos; +0.077 over ridge on FLIP2
key_results.notes: Untuned equal-weight rank average beats both models with intervals excluding zero, showing complementary error profiles.

key_results.benchmark: 7 FLIP2 probe splits (k=256 controls)
key_results.baseline_model: One-hot ridge 0.209 (vs cipher); ESMC-6B zero-shot 0.318 (vs k0)
key_results.baseline_score: Cipher beats one-hot ridge by +0.070; k0_described 0.391 vs ESMC-6B 0.318
key_results.notes: Separates true in-context learning (flipped reverses to -0.235 on 6/8 sets; cipher retains 0.278) from prior protein knowledge (Rhomax stays +0.583 when flipped and drops to -0.020 under cipher).

temporal_cutoff.evidence: FLIP2 predates the June 2026 cutoff (Zenodo 2026-01-30), so the experiment explicitly pairs FLIP2 with post-cutoff MaveDB urn:mavedb:00001329-a-3 (published 2026-11-20) plus k0_recall exact-match tests (0/400 exact continuous matches).

homology_overlap.evidence: Evaluates FLIP2's extrapolation splits (by_position, close_to_far, low_to_high, unseen wild-types/proteins) and FGFR2 by_position; post-cutoff coverage is currently one protein (FGFR2), motivating our post-cutoff MaveDB expansion.

cross_modal_literature_recall.evidence: Explicitly quantified via dataset recognition probe (Mythos named all 7 FLIP2 proteins/studies, unnamed FGFR2 source), k256_cipher (drops probe mean 0.496 -> 0.278), k256_flipped (exposes Rhomax prior reliance at +0.583), and k0_recall.

preprocessing_artifacts.evidence: All methods train on identically rounded prompt labels; exact-match pools separate discrete (nucb, rhomax) from continuous splits; Mythos subagent harness route is kept strictly separate from public API models.

downstream_oracle_filtering.evidence: Direct variant ranking without generative candidate filtering.

compute_and_tool_asymmetry.evidence: Zero tools or code execution permitted (verified via transcript audit); validation-selected low effort reported alongside high-effort sweep (+0.027, CI includes zero); API and subagent routes never mixed.

baseline_fairness.evidence: Nine ridge baselines across ESM-2 650M and ESMC 300M/600M/6B fit on identical 256 rows plus five negative controls; note best ridge is chosen on test queries (favoring baselines) and no fine-tuned ESMC baseline was run yet.

data_and_wetlab_transparency.evidence: All code, exact prompt files, model answers, audit scripts, and tables are publicly released; limitation: Mythos 5.2 ran 100 queries per split (1 draw, 1 answer) due to usage limits.

critiques_and_commentary.author: Anthony Gitter
critiques_and_commentary.summary: Cited as an exemplar of rigorous in-context controls and post-cutoff DMS curation in contrast to OpenAI's unaudited ProteinGym benchmark.

studies.takeaway: With 256 labeled variants and no tools, Claude Mythos 5.2 ties the best ESMC ridge on both FLIP2 (0.380 vs 0.367) and a post-cutoff FGFR2 screen (0.561 vs 0.572), and averaging their rankings beats both (0.443 / 0.611). Prompt controls show roughly half the score comes from genuine in-context learning and half from prior protein knowledge, with Rhomax driven entirely by prior knowledge.

studies.title: Proteins Without Tools: Folding and Binding Physics in Frontier Reasoning Models
studies.authors: Talu Guloglu
plm_baselines: ESMFold-2 -> SaProt 650M & ESM-2 650M (Task 5 monomer alanine scan)
Boltz-2 -> StaB-ddG (zero SKEMPI training) & ESM-2 650M (Task 6 interface alanine scan)
studies.code_and_data_released: Public GitHub repository with all 582 targets, anti-cheat/leakage pytest suite, and JSON result reports across all 8 tasks.

methods.datasets: 582 datapoints across 8 tasks: T1 forward folding (100 PDBs across 5 novelty strata), T2 inverse folding (same 100 stripped CA-only UNK backbones), T3 remote homology (120 SCOPe pairs across 3 difficulty rungs + decoys), T4 CAFA-6 function (120 UniProt entries in 2x3 pre/post-May-2026 x NK/LK/PK), T5 monomer alanine scan (52 panels x 18 = 936 mutations incl. 12 post-cutoff MaveDB & 24 de novo), T6 interface alanine scan (38 complexes: 31 pre-2026 PDB, 7 unseen/post-2026), T7 de novo & motif design (40 targets), T8 closed-loop AF2 binder design (12 epitopes x 16 shots).
methods.evaluation_protocol: Tasks 1-7 strictly forbid tools, code execution, databases, alignments, and predictors (--thinking-budget 4096). All 582 prompts strip PDB IDs, gene names, organism labels, and MSAs, checked by automated leakage tests. Task 8 runs 16-shot closed-loop AF2 feedback.
methods.controls_included: Pre- vs post-May-2026 cutoffs across Tasks 1/2/4/6/8, TM-score novelty stratification, same-AA neutral decoy pairing in T5/T6 (holding 1D AA-lookup win rate to 50.0% and AA-demeaned rho to 0.000), CAFA-6 Post-NK blind cell, and 5-gate anti-cheat design hygiene.
methods.compute_and_tools: Uniform 4096 thinking budget, zero tools on Tasks 1-7; Task 8 compares 16-shot closed-loop AF2 LLMs vs 16 open-loop BoltzGen samples.
methods.metrics: TM-score, scTM, AUROC & Recall@10%FPR, IA-weighted wFmax, Spearman rho, NDCG@5, Same-AA win rate, AA-demeaned rho, 4/5-gate design pass rate, Hit@16.
methods.wet_lab_protocol: None (computational evaluation on experimental ground truth for T3-T6 and refolding oracles for T1/T2/T7/T8).

key_results.benchmark: Tasks 1 & 2: 100 PDB monomers across 5 novelty strata (no tools, no IDs)
key_results.llm_model: GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6.2 Sol, GPT-6.2 Astra (think 4096, zero tools)
key_results.llm_score: Forward folding: all 3 models < 0.50 TM; Inverse folding: 0.43-0.46 scTM
key_results.baseline_score: ESMFold-2 0.8853 TM (0.8240 on struct_novel); ProteinMPNN 0.88-0.94 scTM
key_results.notes: Crucial tool-free counterpoint to OpenAI's GPT-6 preprint: stripping code execution, IDs, and AFDB relaxation artifacts drops GPT-6.2 inverse folding to 0.43-0.46 scTM vs ProteinMPNN 0.88-0.94.

key_results.benchmark: Task 3: 120 SCOPe 2.08 pairs (seq-easy, Foldseek 9-14% ID, deep twilight 8-16% ID, decoys)
key_results.llm_model: GPT-6.2 Astra / GPT-6.2 Sol / GPT-6.1 Sol
key_results.notes: Impressive win over ESM-2 650M on every rung, though SCOPe 2.08 sequences predate GPT-6 training cutoffs so pretraining exposure to SCOPe families cannot be fully excluded.

key_results.benchmark: Task 4: CAFA-6 function prediction (Post-NK blind cell, May-Oct 2026, n=20)
key_results.baseline_score: Pre-NK 0.5497 -> Post-NK 0.4521 (beats all LLMs by ~0.07-0.08 on blind Post-NK)
key_results.notes: Clean temporal-leakage demonstration: GPT-6.2 Astra beats NetGO 4.0 pre-cutoff (0.597 vs 0.550) but collapses -0.224 below NetGO 4.0 (0.373 vs 0.452) on truly unseen Post-NK proteins.

key_results.benchmark: Tasks 5 & 6: Monomer (52 panels) & Interface (38 complexes) alanine scanning with same-AA decoys
key_results.metric: Spearman rho / Same-AA win / AA-demeaned rho
key_results.llm_score: T5 overall: rho 0.494 (AA-demeaned 0.215, same-AA win 58.1%); T5 post-cutoff MaveDB (n=12): rho 0.144; T6 interface: pre-2026 rho 0.515 (demeaned 0.436) -> unseen/post-2026 (n=7) rho 0.163 (demeaned -0.038)
key_results.baseline_score: T5 SaProt: overall rho 0.478 (AA-demeaned 0.461, same-AA win 70.7%), post-cutoff MaveDB rho 0.328; T6 ESM-2 on unseen/post-2026: rho 0.159 (AA-demeaned 0.336, same-AA win 63.7%)
key_results.notes: Same-AA decoy controls expose the mechanism: GPT-6.2 scores high overall on T5 mainly via 1D residue-type priors (AA-demeaned rho 0.215 vs SaProt 0.461) and collapses on unseen/post-2026 interfaces (AA-demeaned -0.038 vs pre-2026 +0.436).

key_results.benchmark: Tasks 7 (40 fold/motif designs, zero tools) & 8 (12 epitopes x 16 AF2 closed-loop shots)
key_results.llm_model: GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6.2 Sol, GPT-6.2 Astra
key_results.llm_score: T7: 0.0% across all 3 models (fold TM>=0.50: 0.0%); T8: 0.0% Hit@16 across all 3 models (best ipTM 0.125-0.262)
key_results.baseline_score: T7: 5.0% 4-gate pass (fold TM>=0.50: 100%, motif<=1A: 62.5%); T8: BoltzGen 8.33% Hit@16 (mean traj 0.542 vs LLM 0.34-0.43)
key_results.notes: Shows that without Python geometry scripts and SolubleMPNN, GPT-6.2 fails every single de novo fold/motif design and 16-shot AF2 binder campaign under strict anti-cheat gates.

temporal_cutoff.evidence: Explicit pre- vs post-May-2026 stratification across Tasks 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, and 8 directly exposes memorization drops (CAFA-6 Post-NK -0.224; T6 unseen interfaces 0.515 -> 0.163); note T3 SCOPe 2.08 and T5 MegaScale de novo predate May 2026.

homology_overlap.evidence: Groups T1/T2 targets into 5 TM-score novelty strata (incl. 18 struct_novel TM < 0.53 and 28 de novo) and isolates twilight-zone homology in T3.

cross_modal_literature_recall.evidence: Strips PDB IDs, gene names, organism labels, and MSAs across all 582 prompts, verified by automated pytest anti-cheat/leakage checks; flags LK/PK literature persistence in T4.

preprocessing_artifacts.evidence: Same-AA neutral decoys cleanly separate 1D residue priors from 3D context; 5-gate hygiene blocks repeat-rod cheating in T7; minor T6 parse failures (89.5-92.1% parse ok) transparently logged.

downstream_oracle_filtering.evidence: Tasks 1-7 use zero external tools/oracles during generation; Task 8 explicitly tests 16-shot AF2 closed-loop feedback and still observes 0% Hit@16.

compute_and_tool_asymmetry.evidence: Uniform 4096 thinking budget and zero tools on Tasks 1-7 across all 3 GPT-6 models; Task 8 actually favors LLMs (closed-loop AF2 vs open-loop BoltzGen) yet LLMs still score 0%.

baseline_fairness.evidence: Strong dedicated specialist baselines on every task (ESMFold-2, ProteinMPNN, ESM-2 650M, NetGO 4.0, SaProt 650M, zero-SKEMPI StaB-ddG, RFdiffusion3+ProteinMPNN, BoltzGen).

data_and_wetlab_transparency.evidence: All 582 targets, prompts, anti-cheat tests, and JSON result reports are public on GitHub (caveat: single inference run n=1, small post-cutoff subgroups n=7 in T6 / n=20 in T4 Post-NK, and computational only).

studies.takeaway: Across 582 identifier-stripped, cutoff-stratified targets without tools, GPT-6.2 models fail forward folding (<0.50 TM), inverse folding (0.43-0.46 scTM vs ProteinMPNN 0.88-0.94), de novo design (0%), and closed-loop binder design (0%), and collapse on post-cutoff CAFA-6 function (-0.224) and unseen interface scans (AA-demeaned rho -0.038). Same-AA decoy controls show their monomer alanine ranking relies heavily on 1D amino-acid priors rather than 3D physics, while they beat ESM-2 650M on SCOPe twilight-zone homology (0.893 vs 0.756 AUROC).

studies.title: GPT-6 as a Universal Foundation Model for Protein Biology: Beyond Specialized Models
studies.authors: Masatoshi Uehara, Edward Zhou, Joshua Park, Morgan Griffiths, Austin Clyde, Suyash Shringarpure, Yuan Yuan, Kevin Rao, Anton Bushuiev, Michael Yu, Kathryn M. Collins, Jesse Hendricks, Puwanat Sangkhapreecha, Lee-Shin Chu, Sharrol Bachas, Joy Jiao (OpenAI Life Science Team and Onava AI)
studies.code_and_data_released: No code, prompts, designed sequences, structures, or full BLI sensorgram tables released; only selected sensorgram plots and trajectory summaries in the 183-page PDF.

methods.datasets: In silico: classic protein/nucleic-acid/small-molecule binder targets, MotifBench (30 motifs), CATH PDB domains (399-400), RCSB PDB & AFDB monomers/multimers, SAbDab antibodies, PoseBusters, SCARPiNo, ProteinGym, Mega-Scale, BindingGYM, Open AlphaSeq. Wet lab (Onava AI): 5 de novo minibinder targets (PD-L1, IL-7Ra, TrkA, VEGF-A, IL-17A), nonpublic minibinder backbones (PD-L1, IL-7Ra, PD-1, VEGF-A, MDM2), nonpublic IL-4Ra VHH complexes (ESMC Binder parents), and 6 therapeutic PD-1/PD-L1 antibodies.
methods.evaluation_protocol: Sections 2-4 allow GPT to write and execute arbitrary Python code (including RDKit + MMFF in blind docking) without internet or pretrained protein models; Section 5 (variant effect, 50-variant ranking) forbids code tools. All wet-lab campaigns use pre-release GPT-6.2 filtered through a 3-model ensemble (ESMFold2 + Boltz-2 + OpenDDE; >=2/3 passing ipSAE >= 0.50 and RMSD cuts); de novo minibinders assign all sequences with SolubleMPNN (8/backbone).
methods.controls_included: SE(3) rotation/translation invariance test on 252 inverse-folding assemblies (Pearson r=0.957), molecular-context ablation (+/- partner), uniform random mutation control for 75-85% redesign, withheld parental sequences on nonpublic backbones in wet lab, and plate control binders in BLI. No temporal cutoff, no homology split, and no matched wet-lab baseline (RFdiffusion/MPNN through the same 3-model filter).
methods.compute_and_tools: Unmatched test-time token budgets and Python optimization scripts (e.g., 120,000 CDR draws in 1CIC, 980 docking starts in 1BGS, RDKit + MMFF in blind docking) vs single-pass specialist baselines; Fig 7C explicitly notes settings are not compute matched.
methods.metrics: In silico: ipTM, ipSAE, scRMSD, motif RMSD, TM-score, lDDT, DockQ, ligand RMSD, torsion MAE, Spearman rho. Wet lab: primarily single-dose 1 uM cell-free Gator BLI hit rate plus limited multi-concentration BLI dose-response curves.
methods.wet_lab_protocol: Twist DNA synthesis, Onava cell-free expression, single-dose 1 uM Gator BLI screening (1:1 fit; calibrated across 289 historical matched hits at Pearson r=0.61, Spearman r_s=0.66, median 3.04-fold error, Appendix B.5), with selected follow-up 2-fold serial-dilution BLI titrations.

key_results.benchmark: Nonpublic minibinder & IL-4Ra VHH backbones (Onava wet lab, 1 uM BLI)
key_results.metric: Single-dose BLI hit rate & dose-response KD
key_results.llm_score: 123 minibinder hits across 5 targets (MDM2 75/88=85.2%, VEGF-A 26/42=61.9%, IL-7Ra 5/18, PD-1 8/59, PD-L1 9/89; 38 hits at 30-50% parent ID); 128/182 (70.3%) IL-4Ra VHH hits (median 46.0% CDR ID; VHH 054/150 KD 10.3-21.8 nM at 17/25 mutations)

key_results.baseline_model: No matched wet-lab RFdiffusion + SolubleMPNN control
key_results.notes: Demonstrates code-generated backbones can yield nM binders, but SolubleMPNN designed all sequences and a 3-model specialized oracle ensemble selected candidates with no matched RFdiffusion wet-lab baseline.

key_results.benchmark: RCSB PDB and AFDB monomer folding
key_results.notes: Clear negative finding: despite code execution and potential PDB/AFDB exposure, global de novo structure prediction remains far behind specialized folding models.

key_results.benchmark: PoseBusters and SCARPiNo blind small-molecule docking (with sidechains)

key_results.llm_score: 0.34 A (PoseBusters) / 0.43 A (SCARPiNo); Scarpino 97.2% success (GPT-6.2 92.1%, GPT-6 91.1%, GPT-5.6 34.1%)
key_results.notes: No cutoff or homology audit; Section 6.3.4 explicitly shows pocket/cofactor recall (Ala80 kinase hinge in 6ZCY, Mg/ANP in 7UY4) plus supplied covalent Cys attachments in SCARPiNo and unmatched RDKit + MMFF optimization vs single-pass DiffDock-L.

key_results.llm_score: Approaches ~95-100% recovery on AFDB and near 1.0 on many PDB entries; refold TM-score comparable or slightly below ProteinMPNN

temporal_cutoff.evidence: Zero temporal cutoffs or post-cutoff computational holdouts appear anywhere in the 183-page PDF (`cutoff`, `leak`, `contamination`, `training data` each have 0 hits); Section 3.1.1 concedes generalization must be tested on unseen nonpublic structures but does not run that computational test.

homology_overlap.evidence: No sequence or structural homology stratification against training corpora is reported on PDB, AFDB, SAbDab, PoseBusters, SCARPiNo, or DMS benchmarks; wet-lab inverse folding uses nonpublic binder backbones on well-known human targets.

cross_modal_literature_recall.evidence: Section 6 explicitly documents recalling protein families, templates, and exact pocket chemistry from pretraining: sequence prefix/template pasting (Sec 6.2.1), barnase-barstar/trypsin-inhibitor/SOD1 docking (Sec 6.3.3), Ala80 kinase hinge and Mg/ANP pockets in blind docking (Sec 6.3.4), and exact cofactor distances in 2WJH (Sec 6.3.1).

preprocessing_artifacts.evidence: Section 3.1.1 (p. 17) admits the internal model recovered 95-100% of AFDB sequences by detecting AlphaFold relaxation geometry artifacts; multimer docking uses bound (holo) crystal conformations (Sec 4.2).

downstream_oracle_filtering.evidence: All wet-lab campaigns filter thousands of designs (e.g., 9,902 passing VHHs, 10,105 passing antibody redesigns with pass rates down to 0.14%) through a 3-model specialized oracle ensemble (ESMFold2 + Boltz-2 + OpenDDE, Sec 8.3), and SolubleMPNN designs all de novo minibinder sequences (Sec 2.5).

compute_and_tool_asymmetry.evidence: GPT writes and executes iterative Python search scripts (120,000 loop draws in 1CIC, 980 starts in 1BGS, RDKit + MMFF minimization in blind docking, footnote 2 p. 47) at unmatched completion-token budgets (Fig 7C admits settings are not compute matched) vs single-pass specialists.

baseline_fairness.evidence: No matched wet-lab control (RFdiffusion/ProteinMPNN/AbMPNN through the same 3-model filter and Onava BLI assay); in silico 75-85% redesign compares only against uniform random mutations (Sec 3.1.4); ProteinGym compares potentially exposed GPT-6 only to zero-shot ESM2-650M; undefined 'internal models' drive most computational wins.

data_and_wetlab_transparency.evidence: Most headline wet-lab hit rates are single-dose 1 uM cell-free BLI (Appendix B.5 calibration: r=0.61, r_s=0.66, 3.04-fold median error) with only a few dose-response traces shown and censored <1 pM fits; no sequences, structures, code, or raw sensorgrams are released, and 'internal models' are completely undisclosed.

critiques_and_commentary.author: Anthony Gitter
critiques_and_commentary.summary: 17-post critique questioning unaudited training-data overlap across PoseBusters/SCARPiNo (~100%), AFDB inverse folding (~100%), and ProteinGym; contrasting with PG-LLM, Rowan, Hallee FLIP2 controls, Boltz binder evaluation standards, and Anthropic's open data release; highlighting opaque internal models and sparse single-replicate BLI reporting.

studies.takeaway: OpenAI's GPT-6 preprint demonstrates genuine natural-language steerability and real wet-lab binding hits on nonpublic inverse-folding backbones (including 10-22 nM IL-4Ra VHHs with 17/25 CDR mutations), while confirming global monomer folding remains weak (TM-score 0.25-0.38 vs ESMFold2 0.80-0.93). However, near-100% computational scores on docking, inverse folding, and ProteinGym are fatally confounded by unaudited leakage, documented template/pocket recall, AFDB relaxation artifacts, RDKit/MMFF search asymmetry, and undisclosed internal models, and all wet-lab campaigns lack matched RFdiffusion/MPNN controls through the same 3-model specialized oracle filter.

studies.title: CheckLLMfold: Contact Map, 3D Folding, Recognition, and Next-AA Audits of Claude Fable 5.2

key_results.benchmark: 4 famous PDBs (1UBQ, 256B, 1TEN, 2TRX) vs 3 no-PDB-relative bacterial DUFs
key_results.llm_model: Claude Fable 5.2 (full fold() protocol & single-reply oneshot)
key_results.baseline_model: Chance contact density (0.022-0.064) / fold() native-contact ceiling (TM 0.61-0.84)
key_results.baseline_score: DUF2489 chance 0.022, DUF2958 chance 0.052, DUF4288 chance 0.032

key_results.benchmark: 48 new proteins (70-95% ID to old UniProtKB relatives, 192 sites) + UniRef50 cluster-size re-analysis
key_results.metric: Old-relative vs new-protein residue prediction at divergent sites
key_results.llm_score: At divergent sites where old relative is known (n=29): predicts OLD relative 59% vs NEW residue 7%; Tu & Chen gap scales from +54.1 (UniRef50 >50) to +36.4 (cluster=1) to +22.1 (post-cutoff)
key_results.notes: Directly shows Fable 5.2 predicts from remembered UniProt family relatives (59% old relative vs 7% new divergence) while scaling like a protein language model across UniRef50 cluster sizes.

temporal_cutoff.evidence: Explicitly contrasts pre-cutoff famous PDBs, no-PDB-relative DUFs, and post-cutoff new proteins diverging from old UniProtKB relatives (59% old vs 7% new).

compute_and_tool_asymmetry.evidence: Directly ablates iterative fold() scripts against single-reply no-tools oneshot.py, showing equal contact precision.

data_and_wetlab_transparency.evidence: All scripts, summary.tsv, transcripts, and rebuilt PDBs are MIT-licensed on GitHub (with AI-drafting caveat clearly stated).

studies.title: A Systematic Comparison of In-Context Learning Strategies for Peptide Property Predictions in Low-Data Regimes
studies.authors: Jiantao Zhao, Andrei Voinea, Mathijs F. J. Mabesoone (Radboud University)
plm_baselines: None (baselines are XGBoost on positional one-hot tokens, TabPFN v2, and TabFM)
studies.code_and_data_released: Full code on GitHub (BigChemistry-RobotLab/icl-benchmark) and splits/predictions on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.23834634).

methods.datasets: 5 low-data peptide classification datasets (151-409 samples): Surface activity (2026, post-cutoff, 409 rows), Beta-sheet formation (2025, 268), Self-assembly (2024, 368), Breast-cancer activity (2018, 199, 3-class), Lung-cancer activity (2018, 151, 3-class).
methods.evaluation_protocol: Single fixed 80:20 stratified split (seed 42; group 5-fold by peptide for surface activity). LLMs/TDMs evaluated one-by-one via OpenRouter (5 replicates) vs local XGBoost/TabPFN/TabFM (100 replicates) with zero-shot and corrupted-label ablations.
methods.controls_included: Post-cutoff dataset (Surface activity 2026), zero-shot vs few-shot comparison, corrupted-label ablation (inverted/shifted labels), and one-by-one vs all-at-once inference check (p=0.2207).
methods.compute_and_tools: No external tools; total API cost $69.43 across 36,562 requests / 146.9M tokens logged in Table S8.
methods.metrics: Macro-F1 with 2,000-resample test bootstrap comparing #1 vs #2 models per task (Table S10).

key_results.benchmark: 5 low-data peptide classification datasets (151-409 rows)
key_results.baseline_score: Surface XGB 0.714 (diff +0.048, -0.033 to +0.130); Beta-sheet XGB 0.800; Self-assembly XGB 0.750; Lung TabFM 0.540
key_results.notes: No top model beats runner-up significantly on any of the 5 tasks (all bootstrap CIs include zero). Corrupted-label loss (0.432) exceeds zero-shot loss (0.223) in 22/25 pairs, proving in-context label reliance; pre-cutoff zero-shot inflation (0.546-0.722 vs 0.270-0.397 post-cutoff) flags pretraining exposure on older sets.

temporal_cutoff.evidence: 4 of 5 datasets (2018-2025) predate model cutoffs and show high zero-shot F1 (0.546-0.722 on beta-sheet, 0.665-0.696 on self-assembly) vs near-chance zero-shot (0.270-0.397) on post-cutoff 2026 Surface activity (Sec 3.3).

homology_overlap.evidence: Sec S1.1 states no sequence normalization, deduplication, or homology clustering was applied between train and test splits.

cross_modal_literature_recall.evidence: Prompts name exact chemical systems (C16-tripeptides, buffers, surface tension <50 mN/m), enabling strong pretraining recall on the 4 pre-cutoff tasks.

preprocessing_artifacts.evidence: Kept only minimum surface tension per (sequence, pH), dropped 16 published Houx sequences, and padded variable-length 3-38 aa peptides into positional one-hot vectors for XGBoost (weak encoding for unaligned peptides).

downstream_oracle_filtering.evidence: Direct classification task.

compute_and_tool_asymmetry.evidence: Zero tools; identical prompts across LLMs with complete token/cost accounting ($69.43 total, Table S8).

baseline_fairness.evidence: No pLM embedding or physicochemical/k-mer baseline tested; single 80:20 split per task; positional one-hot XGBoost disadvantages local models on unaligned 5-38 aa cancer peptides.

data_and_wetlab_transparency.evidence: Full code, splits, predictions, and confusion matrices published on GitHub and Zenodo.

studies.takeaway: On five low-data peptide classification tasks, frontier LLMs in context match but never statistically significantly beat even a simple positional one-hot XGBoost baseline (every #1 vs #2 bootstrap CI crosses zero), and no pLM baselines were tested. Strong zero-shot scores on the four pre-cutoff tasks vs chance-level zero-shot on the 2026 surface-activity task directly expose pretraining leakage alongside genuine in-context learning.

studies.title: Does Reflective LLM Feedback Survive a Wet-Lab-Scale Label Budget?
studies.authors: Haoxuan Zeng and Xin Luo (University of Michigan)
plm_baselines: ESM-2 150M + ridge/MLP/GBR predictor with: No edits, Random edits, Local search (1x/5x wall time), Static ridge (Hsu et al. 2022), Fixed greedy/UCB/div-greedy
studies.code_and_data_released: Summary snapshot and validation scripts only; raw assay labels, embeddings, full run records, and controller-call logs are not released (Appendix A).

methods.datasets: 36 ProteinGym single-substitution DMS assays (101,201 variants; 1,500-6,000 variants/assay, <=400 aa, 1 assay per UniProt accession).
methods.evaluation_protocol: Active-learning replay starting at 96 labels and adding 96/round for 6 rounds (384-672 labels in rounds 3-6) on 25% sealed random and position-disjoint test splits (3-5 seeds, 4,211 runs). LLM reads anonymized 5-fold CV diagnostics (no protein names or sequences) and proposes JSON edits to a 15-field ESM-2 150M modeling/acquisition pipeline.
methods.controls_included: Anonymized protein-free prompts, size-matched random edits, wall-time-matched local CV search (1x and 5x), static augmented ridge, one-call (round-1 only) and scalar-only reflection ablations, and Benjamini-Hochberg multiplicity correction.
methods.compute_and_tools: LLM proposes config JSONs only (no code/search); local search explicitly matched to 1x and 5x LLM wall time.
methods.metrics: Primary: sealed-test Fisher z = arctanh(rho) averaged over rounds 3-6 (TOST equivalence margin 0.02). Secondary: top-10% recovery R_96.
methods.wet_lab_protocol: None (offline ProteinGym replay at wet-lab label scale).

key_results.benchmark: 36 ProteinGym assays, 96 labels/round (random & position-disjoint splits)
key_results.llm_model: Claude Opus 5 reflective controller over ESM-2 150M
key_results.baseline_model: Random edits / No edits / Local search 5x / Static ridge
key_results.baseline_score: Random split: Random edits z=0.597 (Delta_z=-0.008, [-0.034,+0.018]), No edits 0.603; Position-disjoint: Local search 5x z=0.506, Static ridge 0.492
key_results.notes: Rigorous negative result: joint LLM reflection gives no test Spearman gain over random edits (p=0.55) or one-shot call (-0.011), and trails local CV search (0.506) on position-disjoint splits. Exploratory fixed-acquisition arm (LLM + random acq.) reaches z=0.647 (+0.043).

temporal_cutoff.evidence: Prompts strip all protein names, sequences, and assay identifiers, exposing only anonymized CV/stratum statistics (Appendix F.1).

homology_overlap.evidence: 36 distinct UniProt accessions tested under both random and 25% position-disjoint splits (Table 3).

cross_modal_literature_recall.evidence: Complete protein anonymization prevents biological literature recall; LLM acts solely on ML diagnostics.

preprocessing_artifacts.evidence: Authors transparently report post-pilot search redesign, validator rejections (Opus no-menu rejected 640 entries across 509/648 calls yet reached z=0.638), and 1 missing Search-5x seed in the 5-seed grid.

downstream_oracle_filtering.evidence: Supervised active-learning replay over frozen ESM-2 150M features.

compute_and_tool_asymmetry.evidence: Matched against 1x and 5x wall-time local search and static augmented ridge.

baseline_fairness.evidence: 20 well-matched non-LLM and ablation arms; only noted gap is missing one-call control for exploratory fixed-acquisition arms.

data_and_wetlab_transparency.evidence: Offline replay only, and raw assay labels, embeddings, and full controller logs are excluded from the released snapshot (Appendix A p.8).

studies.takeaway: In a well-controlled, protein-anonymized replay across 36 ProteinGym assays at 96 labels/round, iterative Claude Opus 5 reflection over an ESM-2 150M pipeline fails to beat random configuration edits (Delta_z = -0.008) or a single round-1 call (-0.011), and trails wall-time-matched local CV search on position-disjoint splits (0.461 vs 0.506). Gains appear only in exploratory arms where acquisition is fixed externally.

studies.title: Guided Inverse Folding with LLMs
studies.authors: Ishaan Ganti (Rowan Scientific)
plm_baselines: ProteinMPNN (T=0.1, used to generate 3 of 4 in-context example sequences; not tabulated head-to-head)
studies.code_and_data_released: Prompt templates and RBFE protocol in appendices; no public GitHub repo or numerical pass-rate table released.

methods.datasets: 5 PDB backbones stripped to N/CA/C/O (all Gly): 4 post-cutoff (9VGJ, 9N30, 27AH, 9TLN, June-Aug 2026) + 1 pre-cutoff (9C14, Aug 2025). Plus a ligand-selectivity pocket redesign case study on 5WGD (240 aa) against estradiol (E2), estrone (E1), and testosterone (T).
methods.evaluation_protocol: Because zero-shot inverse folding failed in pilots, every prompt provides 4 compatible sequences (1 PDB reference + 3 ProteinMPNN T=0.1 sequences) and enforces <=70%, 50%, or 40% sequence identity caps against examples and within-batch (not across rounds). 3 rounds x 6 proposals in a closed-book Python 3.11 sandbox with ESMFold2/Boltz-2 refolding metrics fed back in rounds 2-3. 5WGD uses GPT-6 Astra to propose 8 sequences/ligand, co-folds with Boltz-2/ESMFold2, picks 1/ligand with fresh GPT-6 Astra, and evaluates via Rowan RBFE.
