methods.compute_and_tools: Closed-book Python 3.11 sandbox (numpy/scipy/pandas) + 2 rounds of ESMFold2/Boltz-2 metrics. OpenAI models ran at High effort with no turn timeout; Claude Opus 5 downgraded to Medium effort with 600-900 s prompt timeouts.
methods.metrics: Refolding pass rate (ESMFold2 & Boltz-2 Ca RMSD <= 2.5 A, TM-score >= 0.80, pLDDT >= 75); RBFE delta-delta-G (kcal/mol) on 5WGD.

key_results.benchmark: 5 PDB backbones (4 post-cutoff June-Aug 2026) at 70%/50%/40% identity caps
key_results.metric: ESMFold2 + Boltz-2 refolding pass rate (plot-only, no scalar table)
key_results.llm_model: GPT-6 Astra / GPT-5.6 Sol / GPT-5.6 Terra / Claude Opus 5 (with 4 example sequences)
key_results.llm_score: Zero-shot failed; with 4 examples GPT-6 Astra leads and produces passing designs at 50% (and 27AH 40% cap: 28/82 ref match); Opus 5 struggles even on 9TLN
key_results.baseline_model: ProteinMPNN (supplied 3/4 examples; no head-to-head pass rate reported)
key_results.notes: Post-cutoff Gly-stripped backbones control memorization well, showing zero-shot fails without examples while guided redesign succeeds down to 40-50% ID; confounded by ProteinMPNN seed examples, lack of inter-round ID caps, asymmetric Claude timeouts, and missing no-feedback control.

key_results.benchmark: 5WGD ligand-selectivity pocket redesign (N=1 candidate/ligand)
key_results.llm_model: GPT-6 Astra + Boltz-2/ESMFold2 co-folding + GPT-6 Astra selector
key_results.llm_score: Testosterone design: +3.16 vs E1, +3.83 vs E2 (cycle disc 0.05); E1 design: +2.57 vs E2, +2.32 vs T (disc 2.01); E2 design failed (-0.71 vs E1)
key_results.notes: Pre-cutoff 5WGD target, N=1 selected candidate per ligand, computational RBFE only (E1 cycle discrepancy 2.01 kcal/mol).

temporal_cutoff.evidence: 4 of 5 main inverse-folding backbones (9VGJ, 9N30, 27AH, 9TLN) were released in PDB June-August 2026 after model cutoffs; pre-cutoff 9C14 and 5WGD are explicitly noted.

homology_overlap.evidence: Zero-shot failed, so every prompt supplied 4 compatible sequences (1 native + 3 ProteinMPNN); identity caps were not enforced across rounds and Appendix D shows models hugging the identity ceiling.

cross_modal_literature_recall.evidence: 4/5 main backbones are post-cutoff, Gly-stripped, and run in a no-network sandbox (pre-cutoff 9C14 and 5WGD remain exposed).

preprocessing_artifacts.evidence: Native reference exempted from refolding filter; inter-round sequence reuse uncapped; GPT-5.6 Terra violated the 70% cap on 3/6 final-round 9C14 sequences.

downstream_oracle_filtering.evidence: 3/4 input sequences come from ProteinMPNN, rounds 2-3 use ESMFold2/Boltz-2 feedback, and 5WGD selects 1/8 candidates via Boltz-2/ESMFold2 co-folds.

compute_and_tool_asymmetry.evidence: OpenAI models ran at High effort without turn timeouts, whereas Claude Opus 5 was downgraded to Medium effort with 600-900 s timeouts.

baseline_fairness.evidence: Authors admit no parallel no-feedback iteration control was run, and ProteinMPNN was not benchmarked head-to-head on the same identity-cap criteria.

data_and_wetlab_transparency.evidence: No wet-lab validation, no numerical pass-rate table in text, and no public repository link.

critiques_and_commentary.author: Anthony Gitter
critiques_and_commentary.summary: Highlighted Rowan's choice of newly released post-cutoff PDB structures as a necessary control missing from OpenAI's GPT-6 inverse-folding benchmark.

studies.takeaway: On four post-cutoff Gly-stripped PDB backbones, frontier LLMs fail zero-shot inverse folding but generate refoldable designs down to 40-50% identity when seeded with four compatible example sequences (native + ProteinMPNN) and a Python sandbox. Gains from iterative ESMFold2/Boltz-2 feedback are small and confounded by missing no-feedback controls, uncapped inter-round reuse, asymmetric Claude timeouts, and purely computational evaluation.

studies.title: Autonomous de Novo Protein Binder Design with Claude
studies.authors: Claude Science and Amir Shanehsazzadeh (Anthropic)
plm_baselines: Orchestrated tools: PXDesign, RFdiffusion3, Genie 3, FreeBindCraft, BoltzGen, RFdiffusion, Proteina-Complexa, FoldCraft, BoltzDesign1, ProteinHunter, SolubleMPNN, ProteinMPNN, ESMC, ESMFold2, Protenix v2
Retrospective Adaptyv competition entries (not matched controls)
studies.code_and_data_released: Full Hugging Face dataset (Anthropic/claude-protein-binder-design, CC BY 4.0 / MIT) with all 1,440 designs, raw CRO SPR sensorgrams, fits, integrated calls, provenance, and the 16,000-word protocol prompt.

methods.datasets: 16 protein targets given by name, UniProt ID, organism, oligomeric state, and cofactors (15 analyzed after excluding aggregating mature GDF-8: TNFa, VEGF-A, latent GDF-8, PD-L1, TREM2, IL-7Ra, TrkA, EGFR, Nipah G, BHRF1, RBX1, SpCas9 RNP, 15-PGDH, de novo BBF-14, E. coli MBP); 1,320 synthesized designs.
methods.evaluation_protocol: Autonomous agent runs a frozen ~16,000-word protocol with bioRxiv/offline literature corpus (including Adaptyv/ProteinBase competition reports), orchestrating >=7 backbone generators, SolubleMPNN/ProteinMPNN, novelty checks vs UniRef90/ProteinBase, and a 5-seed 3-model co-folding ensemble (ESMFold2, ESMFold2-Fast, Protenix v2; 4:1 ipSAE_min : sc-DockQ). Multi-target (48h, $50k Modal GPU budget) and single-target (24h, $10k/target).
methods.controls_included: Blinded dual-CRO synthesis and SPR validation (Adaptyv Bio + Twist Bioscience; Cohen's kappa = 0.71 across 1,235 shared designs), blinded dual-reader trace grading (96-98% agreement), off-target CLEC12A and mouse/cynomolgus ortholog specificity controls, binder novelty check (98% <30% PDB identity), and same-plate re-synthesis of RBX1 competition winner. No matched human-expert control campaign.
methods.compute_and_tools: $10,000 per single-target 24h campaign (2.8x per-target compute of $50k/14-target 48h campaign) on Modal GPUs running 10+ specialized protein generation and co-folding models.
methods.metrics: Integrated dual-CRO SPR binding hit rate, KD thresholds (<100 nM, <10 nM, <1 nM), rank-1/top-5/top-10 hit rates, and mean Average Precision (AP).
methods.wet_lab_protocol: Adaptyv Bio cell-free expression + immobilized single-cycle SPR (10 nM-1 uM duplicate, 1,320 designs) and Twist Bioscience HEK293 IgG1 Fc-fusion 6-point SPR (4.1 nM-1 uM, 1,260 designs) with blinded ordering and dual-reader curve grading.

key_results.benchmark: 15 targets, 1,320 designs across two blinded CROs (Adaptyv + Twist SPR)
key_results.metric: Integrated wet-lab SPR hit rate & rank-1 calibration
key_results.llm_model: Claude Mythos Preview & Opus 4.8 orchestrating open protein generators + 3-model ensemble
key_results.baseline_model: No matched human-expert campaign (retrospective Adaptyv competitions only)
key_results.baseline_score: RBX1 same-plate: Mythos rank-1 KD 3.9 nM vs competition winner 45 nM; de novo BBF-14 3/90; MBP 0/90
key_results.notes: Rigorous dual-CRO wet-lab proof of autonomous tool orchestration (with exemplary open data release), explicitly scoped to agentic orchestration of specialized models rather than intrinsic LLM generation; lacks a matched human-expert control at equal GPU budget.

temporal_cutoff.evidence: Most targets are extensively characterized literature targets, and Adaptyv/ProteinBase competition reports for EGFR, TREM2, RBX1, and Nipah G were explicitly included in the agent's offline corpus.

homology_overlap.evidence: 98% (1,285/1,315) of tested binder designs have <30% sequence identity to any PDB chain (max 56%); however, targets themselves are mostly well-studied natural proteins (de novo target BBF-14 yielded 3/90 hits).

cross_modal_literature_recall.evidence: Agents had bioRxiv access and competition corpora; 91-100% of designs targeted known natural-partner epitopes on 8/10 complexed targets (useful for engineering, but not de novo epitope discovery).

preprocessing_artifacts.evidence: All delivered designs synthesized unmodified; mature GDF-8 exclusion documented; blinded dual-reader SPR grading (96-98% agreement) and fixed integration rules published.

downstream_oracle_filtering.evidence: All backbones, sequences, and rankings come from specialized models (PXDesign, RFdiffusion3, BoltzGen, SolubleMPNN, ESMFold2, Protenix v2); this tests agentic orchestration, not intrinsic LLM protein modeling.

compute_and_tool_asymmetry.evidence: Single-target runs spent $10,000/target in Modal GPU compute (2.8x per-target budget of multi-target runs) across 10+ specialized models, uncalibrated against retrospective competition entrants.

baseline_fairness.evidence: Authors explicitly state they did not run a matched human-expert campaign using identical tools and GPU budgets; competition comparisons are retrospective.

data_and_wetlab_transparency.evidence: Gold-standard transparency: two independent blinded CROs, off-target/ortholog controls, all 1,440 designs, raw SPR sensorgrams, fits, and full 16,000-word prompt released on Hugging Face.

critiques_and_commentary.author: Anthony Gitter
critiques_and_commentary.summary: Praised as a model of scientific transparency for releasing full raw CRO data, designs, and methodology on Hugging Face.

studies.takeaway: Claude Mythos Preview and Opus 4.8 autonomously orchestrated open-source protein generators and a 3-model co-folding filter to achieve a 26.8% dual-CRO wet-lab SPR binder hit rate across 14 of 15 targets (49% at rank 1) with exemplary open data release. This validates agentic orchestration of specialized tools, not intrinsic LLM protein design, and lacks a compute-matched human-expert baseline.

studies.title: Binder Optimization with LLMs and Specialized Models (TNKS2 Small-Molecule Lead Optimization)
studies.authors: Ishaan Ganti (Rowan Scientific)
studies.code_and_data_released: Full tables, prompt appendix, and constraint lists in blog post; no public repo link or experimental validation.

methods.datasets: Tankyrase 2 (TNKS2) neutral phenylquinazolinone scaffold (Ligand 1a, experimental -8.55 kcal/mol; Rowan RBFE calibration R^2=0.411, rho=0.621, RMSE=0.768 kcal/mol); plus an F85Q pocket-mutation control.
methods.evaluation_protocol: 5 structural/chemical constraints + negative docking/MM-GBSA filter; 32 ligands/batch. Specialized baselines run 1-shot only with imposed decoration site/size priors; LLMs run in a no-network Python/RDKit sandbox choosing sites freely for 1-shot AND 4 iterative rounds with RBFE ddG, MM/GBSA, and docking feedback.
methods.controls_included: Wild-type vs F85Q pocket-mutation control (testing whether fluorinated para substituents adapt to pocket sterics), accidental Opus 5 no-RDKit ablation, and cross-method cycle-closure RBFE network check (RMS error 2.59 kcal/mol).
methods.compute_and_tools: 23 RBFE jobs / 739 transformations (56.5 h). LLMs run 4 iterative RBFE-guided rounds with free site selection while specialized baselines run 1-shot only.
methods.metrics: Hub-and-spoke RBFE ddG (kcal/mol vs parent) and ddG per added heavy atom.

key_results.benchmark: TNKS2 scaffold decoration (32 ligands/round, RBFE ddG kcal/mol)
key_results.metric: Top-1 / Top-5 RBFE ddG (more negative = tighter)
key_results.llm_model: GPT-5.6 Sol / Claude Opus 5 (1-shot -> 4 rounds RBFE feedback)
key_results.llm_score: 1-shot: GPT-5.6 Sol -5.44, Opus 5 -3.22 (-4.09 no RDKit); Round 4: GPT-5.6 Sol -9.23, Opus 5 -5.80 (-6.86 no RDKit); F85Q control drops fluorinated para site from 24/32 -> 1/32 (GPT) & 18/32 -> 4/32 (Opus)
key_results.notes: F85Q pocket-mutation control cleanly proves LLMs respond to 3D pocket geometry rather than only reciting PDB TNKS2 inhibitors. However, specialized baselines were restricted to 1-shot with imposed site priors (where CReM and FLOWR beat LLMs), and all scores rest on computational RBFE (cycle-closure RMS error 2.59 kcal/mol) on one scaffold.

temporal_cutoff.evidence: TNKS2 and its PDB inhibitors predate model cutoffs (Opus 5 1-shot designs show higher Tanimoto similarity to PDB TNKS2 inhibitors), partially mitigated by the F85Q mutant pocket control.

homology_overlap.evidence: Single-target small-molecule lead optimization on one scaffold.

cross_modal_literature_recall.evidence: TNKS2 is unnamed in prompt text (inferable from PDB coords), and F85Q pocket-mutation control drops fluorinated para substitutions from 24/32 -> 1/32 (GPT-5.6 Sol) and 18/32 -> 4/32 (Opus 5).

preprocessing_artifacts.evidence: Appendix B discloses a structural non-binding Zn ion was accidentally stripped during PDBFixer prep (post-hoc check R^2=0.86, rho=0.90); DiffDec required OBabel + re-docking while FLOWR bypassed docking.

downstream_oracle_filtering.evidence: Graded solely by Rowan RBFE (Merck calibration R^2=0.411, rho=0.621; cross-method cycle-closure RMS error 2.59 kcal/mol, max 4.33 kcal/mol) with no wet-lab IC50/KD.

compute_and_tool_asymmetry.evidence: LLMs ran 4 iterative rounds with RBFE feedback and free site choice while specialized baselines ran 1-shot only with imposed site/size distributions (explicitly acknowledged by author).

baseline_fairness.evidence: Asymmetric 1-shot specialist vs 4-round iterative LLM comparison; single 32-ligand batch without multi-seed variance.

data_and_wetlab_transparency.evidence: Detailed numbers and prompts published in blog post, but no wet-lab validation and only one receptor/scaffold.

studies.takeaway: On TNKS2 small-molecule scaffold decoration, 1-shot CReM (-7.84 kcal/mol) and FLOWR (-6.00) beat 1-shot LLMs (-3.22 to -5.44), while 4 rounds of RBFE feedback lift GPT-5.6 Sol to -9.23 kcal/mol and an F85Q pocket-mutation control proves genuine structural responsiveness. However, specialized models were not run iteratively, and claims rest on noisy computational RBFE on one target without wet-lab verification.

studies.title: PG-LLM: Benchmarking General-Purpose Language Models for Protein Variant Ranking
studies.authors: Rohit Krishan Arora, Leo Tianlai Chen, Melissa Du, Debora S. Marks, George M. Church (Harvard / Capable)
plm_baselines: 95 ProteinGym v1.3 predictors (46 sequence-only incl. ESM2-650M; 49 alignment/structure incl. VenusREM); ESM2-650M and VespaG on post-cutoff set
studies.code_and_data_released: MIT-licensed benchmark runner, splits, leaderboard, and public reasoning traces on proteingymllm.com and GitHub (note: bioRxiv PDF v3 returned HTTP 429; verified from official website and GitHub repo).

methods.datasets: ProteinGym v1.3 substitutions (217 assays, 186 proteins) plus a post-knowledge-cutoff holdout of 59 assays from 19 studies with variant tables publicly retrievable >= 2026-02-01 (57/59 postdate Sol's 2026-02-16 cutoff).
methods.evaluation_protocol: Each episode supplies wild-type sequence, protein/organism name, phenotype description, fitness direction, and N=50 decile-stratified shuffled mutant sequences (3 seeds/assay); model returns JSON ranking with no tools, MSAs, or structures. Verified from proteingymllm.com and GitHub README (full bioRxiv PDF rate-limited).
methods.controls_included: 59-assay post-Feb-2026 holdout, LLM-judge reasoning-trace audit for source-study recognition (Gemini 3.5 Flash), difficulty-adjusted residual check on recognized vs unrecognized traces, and identical N=50 scoring of all 95 specialist baselines.
methods.compute_and_tools: No external tools; sweeps low/high/xhigh/max reasoning effort (exact token/dollar totals not on landing summary).
methods.metrics: Spearman rho (nested-macro assay->protein->category over 3 draws; study-group macro on 59 post-cutoff assays).

key_results.benchmark: ProteinGym v1.3 (217 assays, N=50 decile-sampled sets x 3 seeds)
key_results.baseline_model: 95 ProteinGym predictors (sequence-only median / alignment+struct median / VenusREM)
key_results.baseline_score: Seq-only median 0.374 (Opus 5 beats 41/46); Alignment/struct median 0.435 (Opus 5 beats 8/49); VenusREM 0.523
key_results.notes: Pre-cutoff benchmark with 88% (Sol) and 57% (Opus 4.8) source-study recognition in traces and N=50 decile subsampling (explicitly not interchangeable with full ProteinGym).

key_results.benchmark: 59 post-Feb-2026 DMS assays (19 studies, N=50 decile-sampled sets)
key_results.llm_model: GPT-5.6 Sol (max) / Claude Opus 4.8 (xhigh) / Gemini 3.5 Flash (high)
key_results.llm_score: GPT-5.6 Sol 0.332 (0.271 low -> 0.332 max); Opus 4.8 0.290; Gemini 3.5 Flash 0.255 (Opus 5 omitted on site summary)
key_results.baseline_score: ESM2-650M 0.202; VespaG 0.323 (no alignment/structure SOTA like VenusREM shown on site summary)
key_results.notes: Strong temporal holdout showing GPT-5.6 Sol drops from 0.402 to 0.332 post-cutoff yet still beats ESM2-650M (0.202) and matches VespaG (0.323) on N=50 sets; caveat: prompts include protein/organism names, homology is unreported on site, and bioRxiv PDF v3 could not be fetched due to HTTP 429.

temporal_cutoff.evidence: Curates 59 assays from 19 studies publicly retrievable >= 2026-02-01 (57/59 after Sol's 2026-02-16 cutoff), exposing a drop from 0.402 -> 0.332 (Sol) and 0.356 -> 0.290 (Opus 4.8); Opus 5 absent from post-cutoff summary.

homology_overlap.evidence: No sequence-homology stratification of the 59 post-cutoff proteins against pretraining proteins is documented on the website or GitHub README.

cross_modal_literature_recall.evidence: Prompts include protein and organism names; reasoning-trace audit finds 88% (Sol, 512/585) and 57% (Opus 4.8, 324/568) recognize the source study on ProteinGym, and authors warn visible traces cannot rule out silent recall.

preprocessing_artifacts.evidence: Uses N=50 decile-stratified subsets to avoid long-context degradation, which the authors state makes scores not directly interchangeable with full ProteinGym assays.

downstream_oracle_filtering.evidence: Direct zero-shot ranking without external oracle filtering.

compute_and_tool_asymmetry.evidence: Uses max/xhigh test-time reasoning effort sweeps (token/dollar costs unreported on site) against single-pass pLMs.

baseline_fairness.evidence: Scores all 95 ProteinGym predictors on identical N=50 draws with identical aggregation; on post-cutoff 59 assays only ESM2-650M and VespaG appear on the site summary (no VenusREM).

data_and_wetlab_transparency.evidence: Benchmark runner, splits, and traces are public on GitHub/proteingymllm.com, but full bioRxiv PDF v3 was HTTP 429 rate-limited so full supplementary tables remain unchecked.

critiques_and_commentary.author: Anthony Gitter
critiques_and_commentary.summary: Highlighted PG-LLM's trace-recognition audit and post-cutoff dataset curation as essential controls missing from OpenAI's GPT-6 ProteinGym evaluation.

studies.takeaway: On 50-variant decile-stratified zero-shot ranking across 217 ProteinGym assays (with protein/organism names and assay context), Claude Opus 5 (0.406) and GPT-5.6 Sol (0.402) top the sequence-only specialist median (0.374) but trail alignment/structure models like VenusREM (0.523). On 59 post-Feb-2026 assays, GPT-5.6 Sol drops to 0.332 yet still exceeds ESM2-650M (0.202) and matches VespaG (0.323), verified from the official PG-LLM website and GitHub repo (bioRxiv PDF rate-limited).

studies.title: VibeProteinBench: An Evaluation Benchmark for Language-Interfaced Vibe Protein Design
studies.authors: Hyunjin Seo, Hongjoon Ahn, Jimin Park, Sungjun Han, Gyubok Lee, Soojung Yang, Cheng-Hao Liu, Joseph S. Brown, Leo Chen, Gina El Nesr, Feyisayo Eweje, Sarah Gurev, Hyejin Lee, Junlang Liu, Zhihui Qi, Gyu Rie Lee, Sungsoo Ahn, Jamin Shin, Sangwon Jung
studies.code_and_data_released: No public GitHub or Hugging Face URL provided in the preprint text.

methods.datasets: 957 core queries (627 Recognition, 120 Engineering [60 rationale-guided + 60 constraint-free], 210 Generation [90 GO-conditioned + 120 binders]) plus 90 auxiliary antibody/RNA/DNA binder queries.
methods.evaluation_protocol: Zero-shot temp=0 (tool-free) vs 30-iteration ReAct agent (with RFdiffusion/3, ProteinMPNN, LigandMPNN, ESM2, BoltzGen, PXDesign, Boltz-2, ESMFold2, AutoDock Vina, PyRosetta, UniProt search capped <=2025-09-01) and unbounded Codex CLI on 30 queries.
methods.controls_included: Strict 2025-09-01 temporal holdout on Recognition and Binders (verified by pre-2021 vs post-2025 binder drop: DeepSeek-V4-Pro 17.5% -> 6.7%), PubMed/Semantic Scholar literature exclusion on Engineering, <30% identity on fold recognition, and evaluator calibration on experimental benchmarks (61.5-80.0% BA).
methods.compute_and_tools: Identical tool-free and 30-iteration ReAct setups across top 5 LLMs; Codex CLI token scaling audited (101x-163.6x tokens on 30 queries); Opus-4.6 and Qwen3.5-9B had thinking disabled due to empty replies.
methods.metrics: Exact-match accuracy (Recognition); sequential constraint + rationale + in silico oracle pass rate (Protenix-v1, Boltz-2, MGnify SaProt stability, pyKVFinder, ESMC GO cosine).

key_results.benchmark: VibeProteinBench 957 post-2025-09 queries (Recognition / Engineering / Generation)
key_results.llm_score: Tool-free best: Rec 82.6% (GPT-5.4), Eng 56.7% (GPT-5.4), Gen 14.8% (Gemini3.1-Pro, binders 7.5%); With tools best: Rec 84.8% (DeepSeek-V4-Pro), Eng 65.0% (Qwen3.5-397B), Gen 23.8% (DeepSeek-V4-Pro)
key_results.baseline_score: BoltzGen 36.7%, BindCraft 20.0% on binders (exceeding all tool-free and tool-augmented LLMs)
key_results.notes: Strict post-2025-09-01 cutoff and literature-filtered engineering controls establish that both tool-free and ReAct-agent LLMs fail most de novo generation queries and trail dedicated BoltzGen (36.7%); caveat: computational oracle scoring only (61.5-80% calibrated BA).

temporal_cutoff.evidence: Strict >=2025-09-01 temporal holdout for Recognition and Binders (Table 10 confirms pre-2021 -> post-2025 drop 17.5% -> 6.7%), and search_sequence capped <=2025-09-01.

homology_overlap.evidence: Fold recognition enforces <30% sequence identity (App C.3), but Recognition, Engineering, and core binder targets do not enforce <30% identity against pre-cutoff UniProt/PDB.

cross_modal_literature_recall.evidence: Engineering excludes targets with prior engineering papers via PubMed + Semantic Scholar queries (Sec 4.2, App D.2), and Recognition/Binders postdate 2025-09-01.

preprocessing_artifacts.evidence: Safety refusals count as failures (Opus-4.6 refuses 35.0% of Engineering, Table 18), and thinking was disabled for Opus-4.6 and Qwen3.5-9B due to empty responses.

downstream_oracle_filtering.evidence: Engineering and Generation pass rates rely exclusively on computational oracles (Protenix-v1, Boltz-2, MGnify SaProt, pyKVFinder, ESMC) with 61.5-80.0% calibrated BA rather than wet-lab assays.

compute_and_tool_asymmetry.evidence: Directly compares tool-free vs identical 30-step ReAct setups and documents Codex CLI token blowup (101x-163.6x, Table 6) and tool-shortcutting (24.1% lower diffusion steps, Table 8).

baseline_fairness.evidence: Includes general LLMs, domain-specialized LLMs (NatureLM, SciReasoner, TxGemma), text-protein models (ProteinDT, PAAG, ProDVa), and dedicated binder tools (BindCraft, BoltzGen).

data_and_wetlab_transparency.evidence: Zero wet-lab validation and no public repository URL in the manuscript.

studies.takeaway: On 957 temporally and literature-filtered queries, frontier LLMs score well on recognition (82.6% tool-free, 84.8% with tools) but fail most engineering (56.7%/65.0%) and de novo generation tasks (14.8%/23.8%), trailing dedicated structure-conditioned binder tools like BoltzGen (36.7%). Even with specialized tools, agents frequently drop constraints or skip verification, though all design metrics remain computational rather than experimental.

studies.title: RosettaSearch: Multi-Objective Inference-Time Search for Protein Sequence Design
studies.authors: Meghana Kshirsagar, Allen Nie, Ching-An Cheng, Fanglei Xue, Rahul Dodhia, Juan Lavista Ferres, Kevin K. Yang, Frank DiMaio
studies.code_and_data_released: Promised on GitHub upon release (Sec 7); no repository URL available in preprint.

methods.datasets: ~400 (394 in Table 3 / 414 in Sec 6) low-fidelity PDB-D monomers, 275 de novo RFdiffusion backbones from Dayhoff Atlas (no native sequence context), and 48 (50 sampled) BindCraft binders.
methods.evaluation_protocol: Inference-time Priority Search / Sequential Revision over 75 RosettaFold3 (RF3, single-sequence no-MSA) calls per protein (3 textual step sizes x 25 RF3 calls; ~30.6 min/protein), guided by local residue-range pLDDT/TM-score/RMSD text feedback.
methods.controls_included: Budget-matched random mutations in flagged regions, Dayhoff no-native-sequence test, independent Chai-1 refolding evaluation, and context ablation table (Table 7). Missing: compute-matched LigandMPNN/ProteinMPNN best-of-75 + RF3 selection baseline.
methods.compute_and_tools: 75 RF3 folding evaluations + LLM search (~30.6 min/protein) vs single-pass LigandMPNN/ProteinMPNN.
methods.metrics: Single-sequence pLDDT, TM-score, Ca RMSD, SR-1 (pLDDT >= 0.8 & TM >= 0.8), SR-2 (+ RMSD <= 1.5 A) under RF3 and Chai-1.

key_results.benchmark: 275 Dayhoff de novo backbones (no native sequence context)
key_results.notes: No native sequence leakage on Dayhoff, showing genuine RF3-guided search gains, but lacks a compute-matched ProteinMPNN-75 + RF3 baseline and Chai-1 cross-check on Dayhoff.

key_results.benchmark: PDB-D monomers (LigandMPNN init, Table 2 & Table 7)
key_results.llm_model: RosettaSearch (o4-mini + native sequence in prompt + 75 RF3 calls)
key_results.llm_score: 20.5% (RF3) -> 5.3% (Chai-1); without native seq in prompt: 11.4% RF3 (Table 7)
key_results.baseline_score: 7.9% (RF3) / 3.1% (Chai-1) for both LigandMPNN and Random mutations
key_results.notes: Native sequence in prompt drives much of the PDB gain (11.4% -> 17.2%, Sec 3.2.2 notes LLM returning the native sequence), and RF3 overfitting cuts absolute SR-1 from 20.5% to 5.3% on Chai-1.

temporal_cutoff.evidence: PDB-D monomers and BindCraft binders predate o4-mini and Gemini-3 with no cutoff holdout.

homology_overlap.evidence: Randomly sampled from PDB-D without homology clustering (RF3 runs MSA-free).

cross_modal_literature_recall.evidence: PDB prompts explicitly supply the native sequence (Fig 10), raising SR-1 from 11.4% to 17.2% (Table 7), and Sec 3.2.2 documents the LLM returning the native sequence itself (Dayhoff removes this).

preprocessing_artifacts.evidence: Sec 3.2.2 and A.4-A.5 document proxy hacking (poly-Ala tails, repeats, safe-residue overuse) and 44% (22/50) trace validation failures (budget violations, indexing bugs), plus minor N mismatches (394 vs 414).

downstream_oracle_filtering.evidence: Direct 75-call RF3 reward optimization exhibits heavy RF3 overfitting: PDB SR-1 drops from 20.5% under RF3 to 5.3% under independent Chai-1 (Table 2).

compute_and_tool_asymmetry.evidence: Compares 75 RF3-guided LLM search calls (~30.6 min/protein) against single-pass LigandMPNN/ProteinMPNN.

baseline_fairness.evidence: No budget-matched LigandMPNN/ProteinMPNN best-of-75 + RF3 selection baseline or ResiDPO comparison (only random mutations are budget-matched).

data_and_wetlab_transparency.evidence: Purely in silico (no wet-lab validation) and code/data not yet released.

studies.takeaway: RosettaSearch shows inference-time LLM priority search over RosettaFold3 feedback improves single-pass ProteinMPNN/LigandMPNN sequences (reaching 89.5% vs 72.4% SR-1 on Dayhoff de novo backbones without native sequences) and beats budget-matched random mutations. However, PDB gains lean heavily on placing the native sequence in the prompt, RF3 overfitting drops PDB success from 20.5% to 5.3% on Chai-1, and no budget-matched MPNN best-of-75 baseline or wet-lab check is provided.

studies.title: Rank-and-Reason: Multi-Agent Collaboration Accelerates Zero-Shot Protein Mutation Prediction (VenusRAR)
studies.authors: Yang Tan, Yuanxi Yu, Can Wu, Bozitao Zhong, Mingchen Li, Guisheng Fan, Jiankang Zhu, Yafeng Liang, Nanqing Dong, Liang Hong
plm_baselines: VenusRAR-Ensemble (unweighted 6-expert mean: VenusREM, ProSST-2048, SaProt-AF650M, ProtSSN-Ensemble, GEMME, ESM-IF1)
studies.code_and_data_released: GitHub link stated in abstract, but Appendix C/D system prompts, Cas12i3 agent logs, and exact Cas12i3 mutation identities/raw assay values are withheld ('Updated upon paper acceptance').

methods.datasets: ProteinGym substitutions (217 assays, 2,465,767 mutations), ProteinGym-DMS99 (31 assays with >99% single-mutant coverage), and wet-lab Cas12i3 nuclease (1,045 aa, 30 single-point mutants).
methods.evaluation_protocol: Rank-Stage profiles protein metadata/MSA Neff/pLDDT and writes Python dynamic weighting over 6 specialized predictors; Reason-Stage pools top 200 variants per model (<=1,400) and audits ranks, pLDDT, RSA, charge, and position diversity. Standalone LLMs also tested zero-shot and 10/20/30-shot.
methods.controls_included: Unweighted 6-expert mean (VenusRAR-Ensemble), standalone LLM zero-shot/few-shot, and random selection. Missing: non-LLM learned meta-ensemble, deterministic biophysical/diversity filter, and wet-lab Cas12i3 control arm.
methods.compute_and_tools: Orchestrates 6 specialized pLM/structure/MSA models plus AlphaFold2 pLDDT/RSA/charge and consumes ~249M LLM tokens across ProteinGym (~912k output tokens/protein, Table 7).
methods.metrics: Spearman rho (ProteinGym 217); Normalized Max Score, Top 1/5/10% precision, and Top-K hit rate (DMS99); HEK293T EGxxFP fluorescence fold-change (Cas12i3).
methods.wet_lab_protocol: 30 single-point Cas12i3 mutants tested in HEK293T cells via EGxxFP fluorescence ratio normalized to WT=1.0; no control arm from unweighted ensemble or single pLM.

key_results.benchmark: ProteinGym substitutions (217 assays)
key_results.notes: Clean demonstration that a standalone reasoning LLM (0.159) sits far below single-sequence pLMs (0.414) and specialist ensembles (0.542); also below random on DMS99 Max at N=40.

key_results.benchmark: ProteinGym 217, DMS99 (31 assays, N=30), and wet-lab Cas12i3 (N=30)
key_results.llm_score: 0.551 Spearman (+0.009 over 0.542 ensemble); DMS99 N=30 Max 68.42% & Hit@5 4.52; Cas12i3 14/30 (46.7%) >WT (up to 5.05x)
key_results.baseline_model: Unweighted 6-expert ensemble (no non-LLM diversity/biophysical filter tested)
key_results.baseline_score: 0.542 Spearman; DMS99 N=30 Max 62.22% & Hit@5 1.29; Cas12i3 control not run
key_results.notes: Almost all global ranking power (0.542 of 0.551) comes from the 6 specialized models; no non-LLM diversity/pLDDT filter baseline or Cas12i3 experimental control arm is run, and prompts/mutations are withheld.

temporal_cutoff.evidence: ProteinGym (2023/2024) predates all tested 2025/2026 LLMs with no post-cutoff holdout (though standalone LLMs score poorly at 0.159).

homology_overlap.evidence: No homology split against pLM or LLM training sets; Cas12i3 is called an orphan protein without reporting identity to engineered Cas12i variants cited in Appendix E.1.

cross_modal_literature_recall.evidence: Rank-Stage supplies molecule name and taxon (Appendix C.1), adding text annotations boosts standalone LLM DMS99 precision (Table 14), and Cas12i3 engineering literature predates the study.

preprocessing_artifacts.evidence: Text claims '367% improvement' on Top-5 Hit Rate at N=40 where 4.73/1.29 = 3.67x (+267%) and Rank-Stage (5.38) actually beats Reason-Stage (4.73); Table 15 repeats identical 20-shot and 30-shot numbers; 1-8 failed error files/run (Table 12).

downstream_oracle_filtering.evidence: System re-weights and filters 6 SOTA specialized protein predictors whose unweighted average already reaches 0.542 Spearman.

compute_and_tool_asymmetry.evidence: Uses 6 specialized models + AF2 pLDDT/RSA + 249M LLM tokens (~912k output tokens/protein) compared against single models.

baseline_fairness.evidence: No deterministic non-LLM diversity/biophysical heuristic filter or learned meta-ensemble baseline; Cas12i3 wet-lab assay has no pLM-only control arm.

data_and_wetlab_transparency.evidence: System prompts (App C-D), Cas12i3 logs (App E.2), exact mutations, and per-variant raw fluorescence measurements are withheld.

studies.takeaway: Standalone DeepSeek-Reasoner scores just 0.159 Spearman on ProteinGym (far behind ESM2-650M at 0.414), whereas an unweighted ensemble of six specialized models reaches 0.542 and LLM orchestration nudges it to 0.551 while improving low-N Top-K hit rates. Missing non-LLM heuristic filter controls, withheld prompts/mutant identities, and an uncontrolled Cas12i3 wet-lab arm leave the causal contribution of LLM reasoning unisolated.

studies.title: LiveProteinBench: A Contamination-Free Benchmark for Assessing Models' Specialized Capabilities in Protein Science
studies.authors: Dingyi Rong, Zijian Chen, Qi Jia, Kaiwei Zhang, Haotian Lu, Guangtao Zhai, Ning Liu
plm_baselines: Domain-specialized SLLMs only: BioMedGPT-R1 (17B), EvoLlama (8B), Evolla (10B). Zero pLM or BLAST/InterProScan baselines.
studies.code_and_data_released: GitHub repository released (Rongdingyi/LiveProteinBench); labels programmatically derived from UniProt/GOA.

methods.datasets: 1,797 four-choice MCQs across 12 protein tasks from UniProt entries first publicly released after 2025-01-01, plus 195 CPI questions and a 2020 subset on 5 tasks for temporal comparison.
methods.evaluation_protocol: Standardized prompt requiring strict '1. reasoning ... 2. answer: [A/B/C/D]' format, tested sequence-only, with 6 orthogonal PyMOL 2D structure images, and with 3Di strings.
methods.controls_included: 2020 vs 2025 temporal drop ablation (Table 4), sequence-only vs 2D-image ablation (Table 5), thinking on/off ablation (Table 6), and 1-shot formatting rescue for SLLMs (Tables 9-10).
methods.compute_and_tools: No external tools; frontier reasoning models use hidden CoT compute vs 8B-17B non-thinking SLLMs.
methods.metrics: 4-choice MCQ Accuracy (%) and strict format Pass Rate (%).

key_results.benchmark: LiveProteinBench (1,797 post-Jan-2025 UniProt 4-choice MCQs, 12 tasks)
key_results.llm_score: GPT-5 60.65% (60.49% seq-only), o3 56.48%, Claude-3.7 51.47% seq-only (47.58% w/ images), Gemini-2.5-pro 47.97%
key_results.baseline_score: 31.83% / 24.26% (30.00% 1-shot) / 22.98% (0% strict format pass rate for BioMedGPT-R1 & Evolla)
key_results.notes: 2020->2025 temporal drop is real (GPT-5 66.76% -> 38.47% on 5 hard tasks), and 2D PyMOL images often hurt MLLMs; however, Jan 2025 overlaps mid-2025 model cutoffs, no homology clustering excludes close pre-2025 homologs, and strict regex parsing penalizes SLLMs.

temporal_cutoff.evidence: Uses a 2025-01-01 cutoff (and Table 4 confirms huge 2020->2025 drops), but Fig 1A itself shows GPT-5, Gemini-2.5-pro, and Qwen-3 training cutoffs extend well into 2025.

homology_overlap.evidence: No sequence-identity clustering against pre-2025 UniProt; Appendix E case studies confirm models solve items by matching conserved motifs and lengths to known families.

cross_modal_literature_recall.evidence: Homologous 2025 entries allow conserved-motif family recall, and 2020 items exhibit heavy memorization inflation (Table 4).

preprocessing_artifacts.evidence: Strict format parsing causes 0.00% Pass Rate for BioMedGPT-R1 and Evolla (Table 12), confounding instruction compliance with protein understanding; 6-view PyMOL images hurt several MLLMs.

downstream_oracle_filtering.evidence: 4-choice MCQ benchmark.

compute_and_tool_asymmetry.evidence: Compares frontier reasoning models (GPT-5, o3) with hidden CoT against 8B-17B non-thinking SLLMs.

baseline_fairness.evidence: Omits any pLM (ESM2/ESMC) or standard bioinformatics baseline (BLAST, InterProScan) and penalizes SLLMs via zero-shot formatting.

data_and_wetlab_transparency.evidence: Experimentally validated UniProt/PDB labels, per-task counts reported, and public GitHub repository.

studies.takeaway: On 1,797 post-Jan-2025 UniProt MCQs, GPT-5 (60.65%) outperforms small protein-adapted LLMs (23-32%) and drops steeply relative to 2020 entries (38.47% vs 66.76% on five hard tasks), while naive 2D structure images frequently degrade accuracy. Lack of homology clustering, partial 2025 cutoff overlap, strict format penalties on SLLMs, and missing pLM/BLAST baselines limit how strongly the gap reflects sequence understanding.

studies.title: Protein as a Second Language for LLMs
studies.authors: Xinhui Chen, Zuchao Li, Mengqi Gao, Yufeng Zhang, Chak Tou Leong, Haoyang Li, Jiaqi Chen
plm_baselines: BioT5+ and ProLLaMA-7B evaluated WITHOUT retrieval; no MMseqs2 nearest-neighbor transfer or pLM baseline
studies.code_and_data_released: No public link ('will be provided as supplementary material upon acceptance'); exact test-set sizes N omitted.

methods.datasets: Retrieval corpus of 79,926 DeepSeek-R1-generated Swiss-Prot QA pairs evaluated on ProtDescribe, Protein2Text-QA, and 4 Mol-Instructions protein tasks.
methods.evaluation_protocol: Retrieves k=4 to 11 exemplars matching MMseqs2 sequence homology + text/QA similarity and inserts them into frozen LLM prompts; k tuned on evaluation benchmarks.
methods.controls_included: Zero-shot vs SeqOnly vs QAOnly vs Dual retrieval ablation (Table 2); 48-case human evaluation (5 raters).
methods.compute_and_tools: MMseqs2 + textual RAG over 79,926 Swiss-Prot entries for LLMs vs zero-retrieval BioT5+/ProLLaMA-7B.
methods.metrics: ROUGE-L and 0-5 human rating on 48 cases.

key_results.benchmark: ProtDescribe / Protein2Text-QA / Mol-Instructions (Swiss-Prot/UniProt derived)
key_results.baseline_model: BioT5+ / ProLLaMA-7B (no retrieval; no MMseqs2 transfer baseline)
key_results.notes: Retrieves Swiss-Prot homologs and text-similar QA entries into Swiss-Prot/UniProt benchmarks without excluding test proteins or close homologs, tunes k on test sets, and omits MMseqs2 transfer and retrieval-matched baselines.

temporal_cutoff.evidence: No temporal split on Swiss-Prot corpus or UniProt/PubMed evaluation benchmarks.

homology_overlap.evidence: Explicitly uses MMseqs2 homology search over a Swiss-Prot corpus to answer Swiss-Prot/UniProt benchmarks without holding out exact matches or close homologs (Fig 6 cites exact UniProt homolog RlmN_AZOC5).

cross_modal_literature_recall.evidence: Both retrieval DB and test sets derive from Swiss-Prot/PubMed; QAOnly text retrieval alone produces most of the ProtDescribe gain (18.29 -> 32.59 vs 35.51 Dual, Table 2).

preprocessing_artifacts.evidence: ROUGE-L rewards copying fixed 4-field Swiss-Prot template wording from k=11 retrieved exemplars; k tuned per evaluation set; test N omitted.

downstream_oracle_filtering.evidence: Descriptive text generation.

compute_and_tool_asymmetry.evidence: Frozen LLMs receive MMseqs2 + text RAG over 79,926 curated Swiss-Prot entries while BioT5+ and ProLLaMA-7B receive zero retrieval.

baseline_fairness.evidence: No MMseqs2 nearest-neighbor annotation transfer baseline and no retrieval-augmented specialized baseline.

data_and_wetlab_transparency.evidence: No public code/data link, missing test-set sizes N, and unvalidated qualitative human cases.

studies.takeaway: Retrieving MMseqs2 sequence homologs and text-similar Swiss-Prot QA exemplars boosts GPT-4o ROUGE-L on ProtDescribe from 18.29 to 35.53 (with text-only retrieval already giving 32.59). Without homology holdouts between the Swiss-Prot retrieval base and Swiss-Prot benchmarks or a direct MMseqs2 transfer baseline, the gains reflect retrieval leakage rather than intrinsic protein sequence comprehension.

studies.title: Large Scale Multi-Task Bayesian Optimization with Large Language Models (BOLT)
studies.authors: Yimeng Zeng, Natalie Maus, Haydn Thomas Jones, Jeffrey Tao, Fangping Wan, Marcelo Der Torossian Torres, Cesar de la Fuente-Nunez, Ryan Marcus, Osbert Bastani, Jacob R. Gardner
plm_baselines: None (baselines are LOL-BO/STBO with peptide VAE, DKT/FSBO, POGPE, SGPE, Optformer, LLAMBO)
studies.code_and_data_released: Unfilled 'GitHub: placeholder' (Sec 4); zero scalar numerical tables for AMP results (plots only).

methods.datasets: 1,000 extinct antimicrobial seed peptides (Wan et al. 2024; 100 held out for validation at >=25% Levenshtein distance, i.e., up to 75% sequence identity), minimizing APEX-predicted MIC against A. baumannii.
methods.evaluation_protocol: Outer loop iteratively fine-tunes GPT-4o-mini (7 rounds) on top trajectories from 200,000-call constrained latent-space LOL-BO runs plus self-augmented sequences (APEX MIC < 8); inner loop uses LLM initialization or few-shot sampling.
methods.controls_included: Untuned BOLT-0 check (fails), multi-task GP baselines (DKT/FSBO, POGPE, SGPE) trained on 5-50 STBO trajectories.
methods.compute_and_tools: ~25,000 GPU hours + OpenAI fine-tuning across ~800-900 tasks (200k APEX oracle calls/task), vs LLAMBO capped at 10M tokens (<100 steps) and GP experts capped at <=50 trajectories.
methods.metrics: Summed normalized APEX-predicted MIC and average predicted MIC vs sample count (Figs 1-2 right; no scalar tables).

key_results.benchmark: 100 validation extinct AMP peptides (APEX predicted MIC, Figs 1-2)
key_results.metric: Summed / mean APEX-predicted MIC (plots only, no scalar table)
key_results.llm_model: BOLT (7-round fine-tuned GPT-4o-mini on ~800-900 LOL-BO trajectories)
key_results.llm_score: LLM initialization and 1-1,000 few-shot samples outperform 200,000-call STBO, DKT/FSBO, POGPE, SGPE, Optformer, LLAMBO in Figs 1-2
key_results.baseline_model: STBO / DKT/FSBO (10-50 tasks) / POGPE & SGPE (5-20 experts); no pLM/AMP baseline
key_results.notes: Severe training-task imbalance vs GP baselines (~800-900 vs 5-50 trajectories), <=75% train/val peptide identity, APEX ML surrogate without wet-lab MIC, no pLM/AMP baseline, and no scalar AMP tables.

temporal_cutoff.evidence: GPT-4o-mini-0718 coincides with/follows APEX (Wan et al. 2024) with no cutoff verification.

homology_overlap.evidence: Sec 4 enforces only >=25% Levenshtein distance (allowing up to 75% sequence identity) between validation and training peptides.

cross_modal_literature_recall.evidence: Prompt injects AMP domain priors ('positive charge, hydrophobicity, amphipathicity', Fig 5); no non-pretrained transformer control on peptides.

preprocessing_artifacts.evidence: Strips non-AA characters silently, omits 75%-similarity violation rates, has 800 vs 900 train-set count discrepancy, and omits all scalar AMP tables.

downstream_oracle_filtering.evidence: Relies solely on APEX ML predictor for 200,000 BO calls/task, self-augmentation filtering (MIC < 8), and evaluation without wet-lab MIC assays.

compute_and_tool_asymmetry.evidence: BOLT uses ~25,000 GPU hours + API fine-tuning across hundreds of tasks, while LLAMBO is capped at 10M tokens (<100 steps) and GP baselines at 5-50 trajectories.

baseline_fairness.evidence: Massive training-data asymmetry against multi-task GP baselines (~800-900 vs 5-50 trajectories) and zero pLM or specialized AMP baselines.

data_and_wetlab_transparency.evidence: Unfilled 'GitHub: placeholder', no wet-lab validation, and no scalar AMP metrics table.

studies.takeaway: BOLT shows in plots that iteratively fine-tuning GPT-4o-mini on hundreds of 200,000-call LOL-BO trajectories enables strong few-shot AMP proposals on the APEX ML predictor. However, an ~18x training-task advantage over GP baselines, <=75% train/val sequence identity, missing pLM/AMP baselines, absent numerical tables, and purely surrogate-based evaluation confound the comparison.

studies.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models on Multiple Tasks in Bioinformatics NLP with Prompting
studies.authors: Jiyue Jiang, Pengan Chen, Jiuming Wang, Dongchen He, Ziqin Wei, Liang Hong, Licheng Zong, Sheng Wang, Qinze Yu, Zixian Ma, Yanyu Chen, Yimin Fan, Xiangyu Shi, Jiawei Sun, Chuan Wu, Yu Li
plm_baselines: None (zero pLM or bioinformatics baselines evaluated)
studies.code_and_data_released: No public repository or dataset URL provided in the preprint; Pfam/Rfam numbers omitted from Table 2.

methods.datasets: 30 bioinformatics tasks including PDB secondary structure sst8 (N=264), PDB inverse folding from secondary structure (N=264), protein species prediction (N=200), RBP binding (N=70), and Pfam family generation.
methods.evaluation_protocol: 0-shot and 5-shot CoT prompting (10-shot for Pfam) at temp=0.2 with BioFinder (QLoRA xFinder-llama38it, 93.5% extraction accuracy) for answer parsing; tests continuous vs space vs newline sequence tokenization.
methods.controls_included: 0-shot vs 5-shot comparison and sequence tokenization ablation (newline separation gives >3x alignment accuracy over continuous strings).
methods.compute_and_tools: Identical text-only prompting across all 6 vanilla LLMs with no external tools.
methods.metrics: Accuracy (species, RBP), sequence/sst8 recovery (%), bit score (Pfam).

key_results.benchmark: PDB inverse folding from secondary structure (N=264) & sst8 prediction (N=264)
key_results.llm_model: 6 vanilla 2024 LLMs (GPT-4o, Llama-3.1-70B, Qwen-2.5-72B, Mistral-large-2, Yi-1.5-34B, InternLM-2.5-20B)
key_results.llm_score: Inverse folding 4.64%-6.95% (near 5% random 1/20 AA chance); sst8 recovery 23.99%-34.31% (best Llama-3.1-70B)
key_results.notes: Clean negative result showing vanilla 2024 LLMs fail text-prompted inverse folding (near 5% chance) and score weakly on secondary structure; 5-shot species jump (4-12% -> 75-82%) largely reflects revealing label format.

temporal_cutoff.evidence: No temporal cutoff applied to PDB or species datasets.

homology_overlap.evidence: Protein PDB tasks deduplicate only exact matches with no homology clustering between 5-shot/10-shot exemplars and test items.

cross_modal_literature_recall.evidence: RBP prompts give explicit protein name and species; 10-shot Pfam generation supplies 10 homologous sequences from the target family (App D), turning generation into in-context consensus copying.

preprocessing_artifacts.evidence: BPE tokenization changes sequence accuracy >3x (Fig 4); 5-shot species jumps 6-20x from label-set formatting; BioFinder still mis-extracts 6.5% of sequences; Pfam omitted from Table 2 with text typos in Sec 5.4.

downstream_oracle_filtering.evidence: Direct prompted outputs without oracle filtering.

compute_and_tool_asymmetry.evidence: Identical 0-shot/5-shot CoT prompting across all 6 vanilla LLMs with no tools.

baseline_fairness.evidence: Zero pLMs or bioinformatics baselines (BLAST, ProteinMPNN, NetSurfP) evaluated.

data_and_wetlab_transparency.evidence: No public code or dataset URL, no wet-lab data, and Pfam/Rfam omitted from Table 2.

studies.takeaway: Six vanilla 2024 LLMs under 0-shot and 5-shot prompting fail at protein inverse folding (4.6-7.0%, near 5% random chance) and reach only 24-34% secondary-structure recovery, while newline tokenization shifts sequence accuracy more than threefold. Missing pLM/bioinformatics baselines, homology controls, and public datasets limit interpretation of the 5-shot species and 10-shot Pfam gains.

studies.title: Large Language Model is Secretly a Protein Sequence Optimizer
studies.authors: Yinkai Wang, Jiaxing He, Yuanqi Du, Xiaohui Chen, Jianan Canal Li, Li-Ping Liu, Xiaolin Xu, Soha Hassoun
plm_baselines: None (compared only against a random-mutation Evolutionary Algorithm)
studies.code_and_data_released: No code or data repository URL provided; prompts omitted for 4 of 5 tasks.

methods.datasets: 5 fitness optimization landscapes: GB1 (4 sites, exact DMS), TrpB (4 sites, exact DMS), Syn-3bfo (Potts model), AAV (ML surrogate oracle), GFP (ML surrogate oracle).
methods.evaluation_protocol: Closed-loop evolutionary search (population 32/48/96 x 4 or 8 rounds, 3 seeds): Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct sees 2 parents + fitness and proposes 1 mutant offspring, falling back silently to EA crossover/mutation on invalid outputs.
methods.controls_included: Oracle-budget-matched random-mutation EA; Hamming-distance and multi-objective constraints.
methods.compute_and_tools: Matched oracle evaluation counts vs EA (higher GPU inference compute for LLM).
methods.metrics: Top-1, Top-10, and Top-50 mean oracle fitness across 3 seeds.
methods.wet_lab_protocol: None (DMS lookup and ML surrogate evaluation only).

key_results.benchmark: GB1, TrpB, Syn-3bfo, AAV, GFP (96x4 / 96x8)
key_results.baseline_score: GB1 5.72 (EA wins), TrpB 0.74, Syn-3bfo 1.85, AAV 0.44, GFP 0.50
key_results.notes: Beats naive random EA on Syn-3bfo and ML surrogates (AAV/GFP) while losing on exact GB1 DMS; zero pLM/BO baselines, explicit protein/position naming in GB1 prompt, and unreported EA-fallback rates.

temporal_cutoff.evidence: Llama-3.1-8B (Jul 2024) post-dates GB1 (2016), GFP (2016), AAV (2021), 3bfo (2022), and overlaps TrpB (2024).

homology_overlap.evidence: Single-landscape closed-loop optimization (though ML surrogates lack OOD validity checks, Sec 4.1).

cross_modal_literature_recall.evidence: Appendix A.3 prompt explicitly names 'B1 domain of streptococcal protein G', WT sequence, exact positions 39/40/41/54, and instructs the model to use its own knowledge.

preprocessing_artifacts.evidence: Algorithm 1 falls back silently to EA crossover/mutation when LLM returns None with zero fallback rate reported; prompts for 4/5 tasks omitted.

downstream_oracle_filtering.evidence: Largest wins (AAV 0.76 vs 0.44; GFP 0.97 vs 0.50) are evaluated solely on ML surrogate oracles without independent validation or wet lab.

compute_and_tool_asymmetry.evidence: Oracle call budgets and initial pools match between LLM and EA.

baseline_fairness.evidence: Compares only against random-mutation EA with zero pLM, Bayesian optimization, MLDE, or AdaLead/PEX baselines, and only the LLM sees WT/task descriptions.

data_and_wetlab_transparency.evidence: No wet-lab validation, no code/data repository link, and incomplete prompt/hyperparameter reporting.

studies.takeaway: Prompting Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct as an evolutionary mutation operator outperforms a naive random-mutation EA on Potts-model and ML-surrogate landscapes (Syn-3bfo, AAV, GFP) while losing on GB1 exact DMS (4.80 vs 5.72). Missing pLM/MLDE/BO baselines, explicit protein naming, unverified ML surrogates, and unreported EA-fallback rates prevent concluding LLMs outperform specialized sequence optimizers.

studies.title: Generalists vs. Specialists: Evaluating LLMs on Highly-Constrained Biophysical Sequence Optimization Tasks
studies.authors: Angelica Chen, Samuel D. Stanton, Frances Ding, Robert G. Alberstein, Andrew M. Watkins, Richard Bonneau, Vladimir Gligorijevic, Kyunghyun Cho, Nathan C. Frey
plm_baselines: LaMBO-2 (314K-param 1D CNN discrete diffusion + ensemble guidance)
studies.code_and_data_released: No GitHub link provided for LLOME or Ehrlich code in paper.

methods.datasets: 4 procedurally generated closed-form Ehrlich integer-sequence functions (f1 easy, f2/f3 medium, f4 hard; stylized after antibody affinity maturation; Appendix A.2.7 checks GA rank correlation against DhfR 0.86, TFBind8 0.89, TrpB 0.73).
methods.evaluation_protocol: Prompting test of o1 and Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking on f2 (8 samples). Main comparison: 10 GA seed rounds (10k evals) + 10 outer rounds x 2,000 oracle evals (30,000 total) comparing LLOME (online SFT/DPO/MargE/REINFORCE on Pythia 2.8B) vs LaMBO-2 (314K) and GA. Hyperparameters tuned on f2 only.
methods.controls_included: Procedurally generated leakage-free functions, integer alphabet removing biological priors, size-matched from-scratch LLaMA 226K ablation (App A.9), exact closed-form oracle, and matched 30,000-eval budget.
methods.compute_and_tools: Matched 30,000 oracle evaluations; Pythia 2.8B is ~8,900x larger than 314K LaMBO-2 (transparently acknowledged and tested with 226K LLaMA).
methods.metrics: Minimum simple regret (1 - f(x)), % unique, % feasible, hypervolume (Figs 3-5, 10-19; no scalar regret table).

key_results.benchmark: Procedural Ehrlich function f2 (8 prompted samples, Sec 6.1)
key_results.llm_score: o1 min regret 0.9375; Gemini min regret 0 once (most outputs infeasible or regret ~1)
key_results.baseline_score: Reaches low/zero regret systematically on f2
key_results.notes: Zero-leakage procedural benchmark shows off-the-shelf prompting of reasoning LLMs fails to optimize constrained biophysical-like sequence functions reliably.

key_results.benchmark: Procedural Ehrlich functions f1-f4 (30,000 exact oracle evals)
key_results.llm_score: Wins on f2 (reaches regret 0); ties on f1 (easy) & f4 (hard); DPO collapses; 226K from-scratch LLaMA matches Pythia 2.8B up to 22k evals
key_results.baseline_score: Wins on f3 with higher diversity/feasibility at 0.01% of Pythia 2.8B parameter count
key_results.notes: Clean leakage-free controlled result on synthetic functions (caveat: no real biological sequences optimized by LLOME/LaMBO-2).

temporal_cutoff.evidence: Ehrlich functions are procedurally generated from random seeds, guaranteeing zero pretraining contamination.

homology_overlap.evidence: Synthetic discrete integer-sequence benchmark rather than natural protein families.

cross_modal_literature_recall.evidence: Integer tokens remove biological identity; from-scratch 226K LLaMA matches pretrained Pythia 2.8B up to 22k evals.

preprocessing_artifacts.evidence: Hyperparameters tuned only on f2 (disadvantaging LaMBO-2 on transfer); DPO premature collapse deflates hypervolume; main tests set a=0 (no non-monotonic epistasis).

downstream_oracle_filtering.evidence: Exact closed-form oracle eliminates surrogate overfitting; likelihood-reward miscalibration explicitly audited (Fig 17).

compute_and_tool_asymmetry.evidence: Oracle calls are matched (30k), but Pythia 2.8B is ~8,900x larger than 314K LaMBO-2 (partially mitigated by 226K LLaMA ablation).

baseline_fairness.evidence: Matched seeding, matched oracle budget, hyperparameter sweeps for both sides, and size-matched from-scratch control.

data_and_wetlab_transparency.evidence: Synthetic-only optimization benchmark (no real proteins or wet lab) and no public code URL in the paper.

studies.takeaway: On procedurally generated, strictly leakage-free Ehrlich functions, off-the-shelf prompting of o1 and Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking mostly fails, while online MargE fine-tuning of Pythia 2.8B (LLOME-MARGE) beats SFT/DPO and wins f2. Yet a 314K-parameter specialist (LaMBO-2, 0.01% the size) wins f3 with better feasibility and diversity, and LLOME remains untested on real proteins.

studies.title: A Fine-tuning Dataset and Benchmark for Large Language Models for Protein Understanding (ProteinLMBench)
studies.authors: Yiqing Shen, Zan Chen, Michail Mamalakis, Luhan He, Haiyang Xia, Tianbin Li, Yanzhou Su, Junjun He, Yu Guang Wang
plm_baselines: None (no pLM or specialized protein LLM baselines evaluated)
studies.code_and_data_released: Dataset and benchmark on Hugging Face and GitHub; no train/test split documentation (Datasheet Q12: 'No.').

methods.datasets: ProteinLMDataset (17.46B SSL tokens from PMC/PubMed/UniProtKB + 893K SFT instructions) and ProteinLMBench (944 six-choice MCQs generated by GPT-4/RAG reading downloaded papers).
methods.evaluation_protocol: LoRA continual pretraining (50B mixed tokens) + SFT (850K samples, 3 epochs) on InternLM2-7B evaluated against 16 off-the-shelf general LLMs on 944 six-choice MCQs.
methods.controls_included: SFT-only ablation (InternLM2-Protein-7B w/o SSL: 58.26% vs 62.18% SSL+SFT vs 54.98% base). No train/test deduplication or sequence-dependence control.
methods.compute_and_tools: Fine-tuned model trained on 50B domain tokens vs off-the-shelf general LLMs.
methods.metrics: 6-choice MCQ accuracy (%).

key_results.benchmark: ProteinLMBench (944 six-choice MCQs)
key_results.notes: Datasheet Q12 confirms no train/test split; ProteinLMDataset trains on PMC/PubMed/UniProt while ProteinLMBench was generated by GPT-4/RAG from the downloaded research papers, creating direct corpus overlap.

temporal_cutoff.evidence: Literature spans up to 2024 with no temporal holdout between training corpora and ProteinLMBench.

homology_overlap.evidence: Appendix Datasheet Q12 explicitly states no splits exist ('No.') and Q13 acknowledges near-duplicate sequences mapped to the same papers.

cross_modal_literature_recall.evidence: SSL trains on 320,000 PMC full texts and >3M PubMed abstracts while ProteinLMBench was generated by an LLM reading the downloaded papers (Appendix Q22).

preprocessing_artifacts.evidence: Automated BERN2 NER/NEN linking, no multi-seed runs, unexplained near-chance Qwen1.5-7B (21.73%), and Table 3 formatting artifact.
